clue.text: Irishman reading stuff current in newspaper?

parts.note: to stuff a cushion is to pad it

indicators.note: the current is set in the middle of the newspaper, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: rag is a slang word for a low-grade newspaper
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An Irishman sits reading the electricity news in his paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reading' only links the definition to the wordplay; it tempts you towards books or the town of Reading. 'in' puts I inside RAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Padraig is the Irish form of Patrick, a common given name for a man from Ireland.

clue.text: Agree to what one might do to unruly hair

definitions.meaning: to allow or consent to something

definitions.text: what one might do to unruly hair
definitions.meaning: read as ..., give it a permanent wave to tame it

explanation.surface: Consenting to having one's wild hair styled.
explanation.definitionFit: Permit is to allow; split, it is the hairdresser's perm applied to it.

clue.text: What will help one stay clean in dodgy stand-up

definitions.text: What will help one stay clean

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or broken, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A comedian trying to keep the act clean in a dubious stand-up routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' rearranges STANDUP; 'in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A dustpan collects sweepings so a floor can be kept tidy, helping one stay free of dirt.

clue.text: Help about element helium separation

indicators.note: about means the help wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: aid means help
a part is an element or component of something
He is the chemical symbol for helium

explanation.surface: Chemistry help on separating helium as an element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'element' looks like chemistry but is simply a part.
explanation.definitionFit: Apartheid was South Africa's policy of racial segregation; the Afrikaans word literally means apartness.

clue.text: Matriarch possibly needs thousand marks extra

parts.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars
M is an abbreviation for marks, as in an exam
other means additional, as in some other help

explanation.surface: A family's matriarch might need an extra thousand marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A matriarch is a woman who heads a family, and a grandmother is a typical example, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Way of getting around remoter areas after boat returns

definitions.text: Way of getting around remoter areas

parts.note: post is the Latin-derived prefix meaning after, as in postwar

indicators.note: returns tells us the word for the boat is to be read backwards here

parts.note: a sub (submarine) is a boat

explanation.surface: Travel to the remote islands is by ferry, once the boat comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' reverses SUB to BUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A postbus is a British rural mail van that also carries passengers, serving villages with no other public transport.

clue.text: Hard dividing an irrational number, which Diophantus once showed

indicators.note: dividing means the hard letter splits the number in two

parts.note: pi is the best-known irrational number
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Splitting an irrational number, the sort of maths the ancient Greek Diophantus once demonstrated.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Diophantus proved something; the definition means his name, written in Greek, contained this letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek spelling of the mathematician's name has the letter phi in its middle, so his name once displayed it.

clue.text: Job, perhaps one dividing half of sheep up

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the letters are read from bottom to top
dividing means the one splits the half-word
half of means only the first four of the breed's eight letters are used

parts.note: the Cotswold is an English breed of long-wool sheep
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A job sharing out half the sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' gives COTS; 'dividing' puts I in it (CIOTS), which 'up' reverses. 'Job' is the biblical figure, not work.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical Job bore his afflictions with great patience, an example of someone who endures without complaint.

clue.text: American boy outside shouting where are hidden presents?

indicators.note: outside means the boy goes around the shouting

parts.note: bub is American slang for a boy or man
a rant is loud ranting, shouting

explanation.surface: A shouting American boy outside wonders where his hidden presents are.
explanation.walkthrough: A bran tub is a British party game: a tub of bran with small gifts buried in it to be fished out.
explanation.definitionFit: Small prizes are buried in the bran of a bran tub, so it is a place where presents lie hidden.

clue.text: Supported small tree that has given up the ghost

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
the tea plant is a shrub or small tree
to give up the ghost is to die

explanation.surface: A small dead tree was propped up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To steady something is to hold it firm, so steadied means held up or supported.

clue.text: Emperor backed an Iranian language, banning son's imperial title

indicators.note: backed means the emperor's title runs in reverse

parts.note: a tsar was the emperor of Russia
an gives the article A

indicators.note: banning means the son's letter is excluded from the language word

parts.note: Farsi is the Persian language spoken in Iran

explanation.surface: An emperor promoted an Iranian language but forbade his son the imperial title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns TSAR into RAST; 'banning' removes S from FARSI to leave FARI.
explanation.definitionFit: Ras Tafari was the title and name of Haile Selassie before he was crowned Emperor of Ethiopia; ras is an Ethiopian princely rank.

clue.text: Speak at length with enough for meeting, no question

indicators.note: no tells us the question is to be left out of the meeting word

parts.note: a meeting is quorate when enough members are present to do business

explanation.surface: Someone speaks at length when there are enough people for the meeting to proceed, no questions asked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes QU from QUORATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to make a formal speech, typically a long and pompous one.

clue.text: Contribution is not properly used thus at first

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: A grumble that someone's contribution was not used properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is what someone puts in to a discussion or project, a synonym for their contribution.

clue.text: Single-minded and certain to hold volunteers back

indicators.note: back tells us the combined letters are read in reverse
to hold means the certain word wraps round the volunteers

parts.note: decided means certain, as in a decided advantage
the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Someone single-minded and sure of holding the volunteers back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold' and 'back' both act: the volunteers go inside first, then the whole is reversed. The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dedicated is wholly committed to one aim, which is what single-minded describes.

clue.text: Is old mattress I found in hollow breaking the rules?

indicators.note: found in means these pieces are placed inside the hollow

parts.note: a dent is a hollow in a surface
taken as written
a bed can mean the mattress itself

explanation.surface: Is an old mattress found in a hollow a breach of regulations?
explanation.definitionFit: A disobedient person refuses to obey, which is to flout the rules.

clue.text: In disrepair, old-time banners unable to be shown

indicators.note: something in disrepair is broken, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tattered old banners that can no longer be put on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In disrepair' rearranges OLDTIMEBANNERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Indemonstrable means incapable of being proved or demonstrated, and to demonstrate is to show.

clue.text: Complain after ancient coin found in rhubarb dish

indicators.note: after means the complaint word follows the rest
found in means the coin goes inside the nonsense word

parts.note: rhubarb is British slang for nonsense, as is rot
the as was a bronze coin of ancient Rome
to beef is to complain

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles after finding an old coin in their rhubarb pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rhubarb' looks like the food but means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Roast beef is a classic British main course, a meat dish.

clue.text: Play I act badly out of character

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are done wrong, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor confesses: I act poorly in the play, which is unlike me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges PLAYIACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Atypical means not typical, so behaviour that is unusual for someone, out of character.

clue.text: Press particular management groups to act

parts.note: to tread is to press down with the feet, as grapes are trodden
THE marks particular ones, and boards are the governing groups of companies

explanation.surface: Urging specific company boards to take action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Treading the boards is an idiom for performing on stage, the boards being the planks of the stage.

clue.text: Helper of St Paul in eastern Tarsus, travelling

indicators.note: travelling means the letters move around into a new order

explanation.surface: St Paul's helper travels in the eastern city of Tarsus, Paul's birthplace.
explanation.walkthrough: Tarsus really was Paul's home town, so the surface reads as plain biblical geography; 'in' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Erastus is named in Acts and Paul's letters as one who ministered to Paul, a co-worker on his missions.

clue.text: What might confer a degree of tact when cutting cold Yankee

indicators.note: cutting means these letters are removed from the tact word

parts.note: diplomacy is tact in dealing with people
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
Yankee is the NATO alphabet word for Y

explanation.surface: Tact as a qualification, when one is cutting a cold American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' and 'when' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A diploma is the certificate awarding a qualification, so it is what confers an academic degree.

clue.text: Sinister rising member of upper house cutting Young Conservatives

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the letters are read upwards
cutting means the member goes into the middle of the young Tories

parts.note: YC stands for Young Conservatives, the British party's youth wing
a peer sits in the House of Lords, Parliament's upper house

explanation.surface: A sinister lord on the rise, cutting into the party's youth wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' works first, then 'rising' turns the whole lot upwards; the House of Lords is the UK Parliament's upper house.
explanation.definitionFit: Creepy means causing unease or fear, close in sense to sinister.

clue.text: Elders apt to get drunk — very drunk

indicators.note: drunk means the letters stagger about into a new order

explanation.surface: The old folk are inclined to get thoroughly inebriated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges ELDERSAPT; 'to get' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastered is informal slang for heavily intoxicated.

clue.text: Raised to desert pack

indicators.note: in a down entry raised means the letters go upwards, reversed

parts.note: to rat is to desert or betray one's side

explanation.surface: Brought up to abandon the pack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' reverses TORAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarot is a pack of cards used in fortune-telling and in certain card games.

clue.text: Mammal's milk, iodine rich primarily

parts.note: to tap a resource is to milk it
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

indicators.note: primarily asks for the opening letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: A list of what is in an animal's milk: rich in iodine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'milk' looks like a noun, but it is a verb meaning exploit.
explanation.definitionFit: The tapir is a hoofed, pig-like mammal of tropical America and Asia with a short trunk.

clue.text: Provide food initially to everyone boarding railway carriage

indicators.note: boarding means getting on, so these letters go inside the carriage

parts.note: car is used for a railway carriage, as in buffet car

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: E is the film and game rating for material suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: A rail company serving food to all passengers as they board the carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater is to supply food and drink, for a party or for travellers.

clue.text: Steer regularly seen around short cattle breed for this reason

indicators.note: seen around means the steer's letters sit either side of the shortened breed
regularly asks for every other letter of the word before it
short means the breed loses its final letter

parts.note: the Hereford is a red-and-white beef breed from the English county of Herefordshire

explanation.surface: A steer pictured among some undersized cattle, and that's the reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steer' looks like the animal in a cattle scene, but only its alternate letters are used. 'short' drops the breed's last letter, and 'seen around' wraps them round it. Hereford is an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Therefore is a connective meaning consequently, introducing a conclusion drawn from what precedes it.

clue.text: Time with old couple

explanation.surface: Spending time with an elderly couple.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple is a pair, which is two of anything.

clue.text: The French emperor's land in Africa

parts.note: les is French for the (plural)
Otho was a Roman emperor in AD 69, the year of four emperors

explanation.surface: A French emperor laying claim to an African territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a small mountain kingdom entirely surrounded by South Africa.

clue.text: Quarrel with one jeweller

parts.note: a tiff is a petty quarrel
any means one, as in take any of them

explanation.surface: Falling out with one particular jeweller.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffany & Co is the famous New York jewellery house, founded by Charles Lewis Tiffany.
